note: Ramond et al. (2023) originally identified Ramond-Elliott syndrome in a landmark cohort of exactly 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families, all presenting with ID/DD.

evidence.text: The landmark study recruited 12 individuals across 11 unrelated families with monoallelic TRA2B variants, all of whom presented with intellectual disability and/or developmental delay alongside frequent microcephaly.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: A total of 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families who harbored predicted loss-of-function monoallelic variants, mostly de novo, were recruited. ... All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: A subsequent case study describes a single additional patient, confirming that the initial foundational cohort consisted of the 12 patients in Ramond et al. rather than 15.

source.title: TRA2B Gene Splice Variant Linked to Seizures and Neurodevelopmental Delay: A Second Case Study
source.quote: This paper represents the second investigation of pathogenic variants in the TRA2B gene in humans, reaffirming the conclusions of the initial study and underscoring the importance of this research.
